text:
julia: Quick RFC follow-up: we keep seeing misattributed rollout metrics when tenant softbinds mutate the resolved variant after rollout weighting. Need a deterministic reconciliation strategy that's low-risk for customers.

sam: Can you sketch the failure mode? Short: rollout expands to weighted variants and writes rollout_token. Resolver later applies tenant softbind and changes model id, so the rollout_token telemetry doesn't match actual serving variant.

julia: Exactly. We tried three approaches internally: server-finalize (server computes final variant and returns it), precedence flag on pins (explicit enum), or disallow tenant softbinds while rollout is active.

diego: Disallowing is user-hostile. Server-finalize requires API changes (response header + client update). Precedence flag seems backward-compatible and small.

sam: Agreed. Proposal: add `precedence` enum to pin and rollout manifests with values `rollout_first`, `tenant_first`, `reconcile`. Default to `rollout_first` for existing data to preserve current canaries.

julia: Explain `reconcile`. I like a middle ground: both hints are considered, but server deterministically recomputes final weights and emits `resolved_variant` in telemetry so billing/metrics align. Server wins ties.

diego: TTL question: if tenant pin TTL > rollout TTL we risk long-lived overrides. Suggest compute effective_expiry = min(pin_expiry, rollout_expiry) unless precedence==tenant_first and tenant explicitly set a longer TTL. Document this as an audit risk.

sam: Also add `expiry_reason` enum for audits: `manual`, `rollout_end`, `tenant_override`, `system_gc`. Store that in pin_resolutions table.

julia: Telemetry changes: add `resolved_variant`, `precedence_applied`, `final_source`, and `effective_expiry` to resolution events. Add a one-time probe: count cases where server_precedence='rollout_first' but client_applied_tenant_softbind=true.

diego: Client libs: emit a non-fatal warn when they apply a tenant softbind but server_precedence='rollout_first'. Keep warn disabled by default; opt-in via DEBUG env var. That way we can measure divergence without spamming customers.

sam: Migration: feature-flag schema-v2. Backfill rules: rollout manifests -> rollout_first. Tenant pins created in last 90d -> keep tenant_first if tenant touched priority recently, else reconcile. Run dry-run counts and only flip behavior after mismatch < 0.5% for 30m.

ops-bot: migration job #10321 queued: pin-schema-v2 dry-run -> will emit mismatch_report to #eng-sre.

julia: Docs: update pin schema with precedence examples, show `reconcile` behavior, and add FAQ: "Why did my canary metrics change?" with migration explanation.

diego: Action items: 1) PR for schema + migration (julia), 2) telemetry spec + kibana saved queries (sam), 3) client shim warn + tests (diego), 4) ops wave plan + dry-run (ops). I'll open tickets and link them here.

sam: One more: add a short-lived compatibility header `X-Resolved-Variant` when schema-v2 is enabled so older clients can pick up resolved variant without full client update. Make it opt-in for staging first.

julia: Nice. That buys time. Thanks all :thumbsup:
